name: Bifrost C# CodeQL quality
description: Public C# structural and quality policies aligned with reviewed CodeQL query identities and engine fact contracts.

policies.severity_rationale: An empty branch or loop body can silently discard a required operation and is often an unfinished or accidental control-flow path.
policies.remediation: Review the empty body and either remove the branch or add the intended operation; comment-only bodies remain intentional documentation rather than a finding.

policies.severity_rationale: An if statement with an empty arm has no useful behavior on that branch and can conceal a missing operation or redundant condition.
policies.remediation: Review the condition and branch intent, then remove the useless branch or implement the missing operation.

policies.severity_rationale: Reusing an enclosing loop's iteration variable in a nested loop can overwrite the outer control state and cause skipped or repeated iterations.
policies.remediation: Use a distinct inner iteration variable, or review the loop conditions and updates if the reuse is deliberate.

policies.severity_rationale: A public static readonly array exposes mutable shared storage even though the field reference cannot be reassigned.
policies.remediation: Expose an immutable collection or return a defensive copy, depending on the API contract.

policies.severity_rationale: Repeating a numeric value that already has a visible named constant makes intent harder to read and allows related values to drift.
policies.remediation: Use the visible named constant when it expresses the same value and semantics.

policies.severity_rationale: Catching System.Exception without filtering or rethrowing can hide failures and leave the program in an invalid state.
policies.remediation: Catch the narrow exception types the operation can handle, or rethrow after recording context when a catch-all boundary is required.

policies.severity_rationale: Throwing the caught exception variable resets its stack trace, so the original failure location is lost and errors become harder to diagnose.
policies.remediation: Use a bare throw; to rethrow, or wrap the exception in a new exception that keeps it as the inner exception.

policies.severity_rationale: A TODO, FIXME or XXX marker usually records unfinished or knowingly broken behavior that the code still ships with.
policies.remediation: Complete or remove the marked work, or move it to the issue tracker and delete the marker.

policies.severity_rationale: An explicit GC.Collect() forces a full blocking collection, which usually hurts throughput and latency more than the runtime's own scheduling.
policies.remediation: Remove the call and let the runtime schedule collections; if a collection is genuinely required, document why and use GC.Collect with an explicit generation and mode.

policies.severity_rationale: Path.Combine discards every earlier argument when a later one is rooted, so a user-supplied or misformatted segment can silently replace the intended base directory.
policies.remediation: Use Path.Join, which concatenates segments without resetting on rooted paths, or validate that later segments are relative.

policies.severity_rationale: Catching NullReferenceException hides a programming error and lets execution continue from an unexpected state.
policies.remediation: Check for null before dereferencing, or use null-conditional operators, and remove the catch clause.

policies.severity_rationale: Calling an API explicitly marked obsolete can preserve deprecated behavior, trigger future build failures, or bypass a documented replacement.
policies.remediation: Migrate to the API named by the deprecation guidance, or isolate and document the compatibility boundary if migration is not yet possible.

policies.severity_rationale: An Equals override that calls the same overload with its uncast parameter can recurse indefinitely instead of comparing the intended value.
policies.remediation: Call the correctly typed overload or compare the relevant fields directly after handling the null and type cases.

policies.severity_rationale: Passing a character to the one-argument StringBuilder constructor selects the integer-capacity overload and often creates an unexpectedly large or invalid buffer.
policies.remediation: Convert the character to a string when text initialization is intended, or pass an explicit capacity when capacity initialization is intended.

policies.severity_rationale: Hard-coded configuration passwords can be exposed with source or deployment artifacts.
policies.remediation: Load secrets from a managed secret store or runtime-provided environment, and do not store plaintext passwords in configuration.

policies.severity_rationale: Empty configuration passwords can disable authentication or leave accounts protected only by defaults.
policies.remediation: Set a non-empty, securely managed password or remove the credential entry and rely on an appropriate authentication mechanism.
